prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Link Inventory Audit — Q1 2025 (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Page title" · longest unbreakable unit 100px · widest one-line content 319px
  col 2: header "URL" · longest unbreakable unit 324px · widest one-line content 841px
  col 3: header "Last checked" · longest unbreakable unit 61px · widest one-line content 96px
  col 4: header "Status code" · longest unbreakable unit 47px · widest one-line content 86px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 720px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 720px wide (column widths sum to at most 719px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 720px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Audit a set of page links and their most recent check results.","tasks":["Find a page by title and identify its URL.","Compare check dates and status codes to locate stale or problematic links.","Associate each URL and result with the correct page."],"relations":["Each row connects a page title to its URL, check date and status code.","The title and URL identify the resource; the last two columns describe its audit result."],"roles":["The header row names four fields; each subsequent row is one audited link.","Page titles are human-readable identifiers, while URLs provide precise destinations.","Check dates and status codes are compact comparison fields."],"keep_whole":["Status codes and date components.","Meaningful URL components and long unbreakable identifiers where space permits.","Words and identifiers in page titles."],"may_wrap":["Page titles at natural word boundaries.","URLs at meaningful separators when supported by the rendering.","Dates between components if the chosen width requires it."],"same_scale":["All page titles share one column scale, and all URLs share another.","The two audit-result columns should remain compact and visually comparable."],"h_vs_v":"Long URLs compete with page titles for a limited width. Extra row height can preserve readable titles and URL components, but excessive wrapping makes audit results harder to scan across rows."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d2r0A, d2r0B, d2r0C.
Measured facts:
d2r0A: column widths [150, 345, 117, 107] px · table 720×580 px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 83, 83, 83, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
d2r0B: column widths [190, 345, 102, 82] px · table 720×580 px · row heights [60, 106, 106, 60, 83, 83, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 2/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
d2r0C: column widths [225, 324, 90, 80] px · table 720×604 px · row heights [60, 106, 106, 83, 83, 83, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 2/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 2 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). This is your first look at real renders: propose at least one improved or alternative design (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or test an important idea you have not tried). "done" is not allowed yet. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
